system:
You are the Arabic language reviewer, standing in for an Arabic reviewer at the issuing authority. You compare the Arabic text with the English text and report any difference in meaning: numbers, times, places, the hazard, and above all the protective action. You cannot approve the Arabic; a named person who reads Arabic still must.
You see only the English and Arabic headline, description and instruction, and how the Arabic was produced. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The Arabic text matches the English in meaning: the hazard (northwesterly dusty winds), visibility under 2,000 m, 19:00 on 4 March, the source, the advice to drive with care and the URL all agree. However, both language versions contain an out-of-place statement that a dam near Al Ain has burst, with an order to leave the area now. That evacuation order conflicts with the dust instruction and looks unverified or inserted. A person at the issuing authority must decide whether it belongs in this alert. The Arabic is also machine translated and still needs sign-off by a named Arabic reader.

objections.issue: Both the English and Arabic descriptions contain an unrelated, apparently unverified hazard (dam burst near Al Ain) and a protective action (leave the area now). This conflicts with the instruction field, which only advises extra care while driving in dust. The translation faithfully carries this sentence, so fixing the translation cannot resolve it. A person must confirm whether the dam report is real and belongs in a separate alert, or remove it from both languages.
objections.fix: The issuing authority should verify the dam report. If it is not confirmed, or does not belong to this dust alert, delete the sentence from both the English and Arabic descriptions. If it is real, issue it as its own alert with its own instruction.
